title: UK Graduate Visa to Stay at Two Years: Who Qualifies?
excerpt: The UK plans a two-year Graduate visa for graduates of high-compliance universities. See what is confirmed, what is still unclear and how to plan your 2027 application.

content.html:
🎓 UK Graduate Visa Update — At a Glance
Announced2026 UK Budget (Reported 28 Oct 2026)
Proposed Duration2 Years for Eligible Graduates
Other Graduates18 Months Planned From January 2027
Eligibility LinkUniversity Compliance + Labor Market Outcomes
StatusDetails Not Yet Published
Work RightsUnrestricted Work Under Graduate Route

What Was Announced

The UK government says the Graduate visa will be set at two years for graduates of "high compliance" universities with strong labor market outcomes. The measure comes from the 2026 UK Budget and was made public on 28 October 2026.

The Graduate visa (Graduate Route) lets international students who finish a UK degree stay and work, or look for work, without a job offer or sponsor. Until now the route was two years for most bachelor's and master's graduates, and the government had planned to cut it to 18 months for applications from January 2027. This announcement would keep two years, but only for graduates of qualifying universities.

⚠️
Not law yetThis is a policy announcement, not a finished rule. The Home Office has not published the criteria, the list of universities or the start date.

What Is Confirmed and What Is Not

QuestionWhere things stand
Is the two-year visa kept?Yes, for graduates of "high compliance" universities with strong labor market outcomes
What happens to other graduates?The planned 18-month duration from January 2027 is expected to apply, pending the final rules
How is "high compliance" defined?Not published. It is likely linked to sponsor compliance measures such as the Basic Compliance Assessment, but this is not confirmed
What counts as "strong labor market outcomes"?Not published
Which universities qualify?No list yet
When does it start?No date given
Will visa or health surcharge fees change?Nothing was announced on fees

Treat any list of "approved" universities you see online before official publication as a guess.

Why It Matters for International Students

  • Your choice of university now affects your post-study time. Two graduates with the same degree could receive different visa lengths depending on where they studied.
  • Time to find a skilled job. The extra six months can be the difference between a first job offer and leaving the UK early.
  • Sponsor compliance becomes a selling point. Universities with strong visa-refusal, enrolment and course-completion records are more likely to qualify, although the exact tests are unknown.
  • Value for money. If you pay £16,000 or more a year in tuition, post-study work rights are a major part of the return.

What This Means for Nepalese Students

Nepal is one of the larger sources of UK student applications, so universities that recruit from Nepal will be watching the final criteria closely. Until they are published, avoid choosing a university only because you expect it to qualify.

  1. Ask the university directly.Ask whether it expects to meet the "high compliance" standard and what its recent visa, enrolment and completion record looks like.
  2. Check its sponsor status.Confirm it holds a UK student sponsor license and is not under a Home Office action plan.
  3. Look at graduate outcomes.Ask for the share of graduates in graduate-level work or further study within 15 months of finishing.
  4. Do not delay a good course.If your course and funding fit, a strong match matters more than a rumor about one extra year.
💡
Keep your documents strongA genuine English test result, a clear study plan and proper finance evidence protect your visa application whichever university you choose.

Other Changes in the Same Package

The same Budget announcements, as reported, include:

  • High Potential Individual visa: expanded from graduates of the top 80 universities to the top 150, with a proportional cap increase.
  • PhD graduates: the discount to visa salary requirements for PhD holders is to be removed, following a Migration Advisory Committee recommendation.
  • Global Talent route: more host organizations are expected to be added to the endorsed-funder pathway, possibly from spring 2027.

The government describes its aim as building the most pro-business migration system in Europe for high-skill workers while tightening routes for lower- and medium-skill roles.

How Universities and the Sector Reacted

Sector voices have given a cautious welcome. A Russell Group representative said it was encouraging to see the government recognize the benefits of international students. Reports say the Home Office and Treasury had not yet commented in detail, so the practical effect is still unclear.

Sources: The PIE News, Times Higher Education.

What To Do Now

  1. Keep applying for the right course.Choose by course quality, cost, location and your career plan first.
  2. Shortlist more than one university.Compare at least three, including their compliance and outcomes record.
  3. Budget on the safe side.Plan your finances without assuming a longer post-study period.
  4. Watch for official updates.Rules will appear on GOV.UK and in Home Office announcements. We will update this guide when they do.
  5. Talk to an adviser.Admizz Education can help you compare universities and plan your 2027 application.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Graduate visa becoming two years for everyone?
No. As announced, the two-year duration is for graduates of high-compliance universities with strong labor market outcomes. Other graduates are expected to face the planned 18-month limit.
Which universities will qualify?
No list has been published. The criteria and the Home Office process are still to be set out.
When will the change start?
No start date has been given. Check GOV.UK for official updates.
Does this affect students already in the UK?
Details on transitions are not yet published. Rules usually depend on the date you apply, so check the final guidance.
Does the Graduate visa lead to settlement?
No. It is a temporary route. You would need to switch to another visa, such as Skilled Worker, to stay longer.
Will the Graduate visa cost change?
The announcements reported so far do not mention a fee change.
